Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-boost-prompt-medium-0171", "row_sha256": "4c4263e9c58e89bcc35803949d6e82f64e9f5819048309f1f23b452f7c87b9be", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you draft a friendly notice for our repair cafe's next session for the community mailing list, around 130–170 words? it's for people who might bring small household items for volunteers to look at. we can't accept large appliances, so please say that clearly without making it sound stern. mention that visitors should bring the item and, if it needs one, its charger. repairs depend on having enough time and the right parts, so don't promise that anything will be fixed. we haven't set the session date or venue yet; leave both out rather than guessing or putting in placeholders. use plain english and a welcoming tone, and make it clear people are welcome even if they're unsure whether their item can be repaired. please include these exact remarks from the planning sheet, not rewritten: “We can take a look together.” and “Please bring the charger if the item needs one.” don't add contact details or other practical information that isn't here.", "output": "Draft a friendly notice for the repair cafe’s next session for the community mailing list. Keep it around 130–170 words, use plain English, and make the tone welcoming. The notice should:

- Explain that people can bring small household items for volunteers to look at, but that large appliances cannot be accepted.
- Ask visitors to bring the item and, if it needs one, its charger.
- Make clear that repairs depend on available time and parts, and do not promise that an item will be fixed.
- Welcome people who are unsure whether their item can be repaired.

The session date and venue have not been set, so leave them out. Do not add contact details or other practical information that has not been provided. Include these exact remarks from the planning sheet:

“We can take a look together.”
“Please bring the charger if the item needs one.”"}]
